newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian shares at eighth record high.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian shares at eighth record high.

text.p: Egyptian share prices closed at an eighth record high on Tuesday, adding another 1.4 percent to the spectacular gains of the last three months.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index ended the day at 367.57 points, up from 362.61 on Monday and 24 percent up since the beginning of the year.
Mills, cements and the the two big real estate companies repeated their recent daily gains, many of them rising to their own record highs since privatisation.
The most active share was Medinet Nasr Housing and Development, which closed 13.51 pounds up at 465.00. Sister company Heliopolis Housing and Development added 22.00 pounds to end at 502.00.

The flour millers, all of them former state companies which have undergone gradual privatisation, led the field with higher prices across the board. North Cairo Flour Mills hit an all-time high of 178.50 pounds, up 8.50 on the day.
Most of the cements followed suit but Suez Cement ended unchanged at 71.80 and Egyptian Tora Portland Cement shed 0.10 to close at 94.50.
Recently floated Cairo Precision Industries made its debut on the market, rising to 100.05 pounds from the flotation price of 85.00. Turnover was 2.82 million pounds.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 600.34 points from 594.75 on Monday while the index for rarely traded "closed" firms also rose, to 245.67 from 241.67.
Out of the 78 shares traded, 42 gained, 21 lost and 15 ended the day unchanged.
